## Purpose
Settings → Tool safety. These routes create, read, update and delete the tool safety rules, which are optional screening rules applied at named points of the code pipeline and prompts.

## Responsibilities
- **`GET /safety-rules`** returns:
  - `rules`;
  - `points`: the places a rule can apply, from `store.POINTS`;
  - `strictness`: the levels, from `store.STRICTNESS`;
  - `summary{active_rules, points_in_use}`.
- **`POST /safety-rules`** (201) takes `RuleCreate{title 3–120 chars, rule 10–1000 chars, strictness="standard", applies_to=[], enabled=False}`.
- **`PATCH /safety-rules/{id}`** takes `RuleUpdate` with any of title, rule, strictness, applies_to or enabled.
- **`DELETE /safety-rules/{id}`** returns `{"deleted": id}`.
- **`POST /safety-rules/turn-off`** returns `{"turned_off": n, ...payload}`.

## Key elements
`_guard` maps errors to status codes:
- `LookupError` becomes 404;
- `SafetyRuleError` becomes 422;
- `RuntimeError` becomes 503.

## Control flow
None.

## Data, state and side effects
Writes the safety-rules table (`app/safety/store.py`).

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- Route policy: rules.view for GET and rules.manage for writes.
- `app/safety/apply.py` reads the enabled rules into prompts.

## Error handling and edge cases
See `_guard` above.

## Nuances and gotchas
New rules are switched off by default. Built-in rules can be switched on or off and tuned, but only your own rules can be deleted; the store enforces this.

## How to rebuild this file
The handlers and pydantic models as described.
